title: Elmwood Commerce — outreach & pilot playbook (scratchlog)
content:
QUICK TAKE
- Elmwood Commerce = mid-market digital-first retail platform (B2B storefronts + headless checkout). Good fit for: search relevance, product descriptions, chat assistant for merchant ops.
- Benefits to pitch: reduce CS ticket volume (automated agent), increase conversion via better search/ranking, faster catalog onboarding (auto-descriptions).
- Risk signals: strict PCI + tokenization rules, they host some infra on-prem for legacy clients, procurement slow (legal counsel flagged previously).

PRIMARY CONTACTS (found via LinkedIn + job posts)
- Marissa Vale — Dir. Product,  marissa@elmwood.com (decision maker on product integrations)
- Tom Reyes — Head of Ops, tom@elmwood.com (buyer/ops constraints)
- Daniel Park — Eng Manager (platform), daniel@elmwood.com (integration owner)
- Potential Exec sponsor: COO (not identified yet)

TECH FOOTPRINT NOTES
- Core stack: AWS (EKS), Postgres + Redis, React storefronts, Node backend. Some customers colocated on-prem through appliance.
- Data sensitivity: payment card data isolated; product + user behavioural data stored in their DB.
- Existing AI/ML: internal recommendation engine (python), experimenting with third-party embeddings.
- Infra constraints: low tolerance for cross-tenant data export; prefer models in VPC or host-specific private deployment.

WHY REDWOOD (positioning bulleted)
- Unified option: hosted for quick proof-of-value, Dedicated / Private for production (fits their data isolation ask).
- Cost predictability: Redwood Dedicated gives committed throughput; helps their finance forecasts.
- Operational observability: token-level tracing and per-route dashboards — good for audits.

USE CASES TO PROPOSE (ranked)
1) Support assistant for merchant ops (CS triage + FAQ). Fast ROI (ticket reduction).
2) Product description generator + variant enrichment (catalog velocity).
3) Site search reranker using semantic embeddings (conversion uplift test).
4) Conversational assistant for B2B merchant portal (long-term).

PILOT PROPOSAL (6-week lightweight)
Scope: 1 use case (support assistant) integrated into a single merchant's admin panel.
Deliverables: model choices, API integration guide, monitoring dashboard, quality evaluation set + weekly QA sync.
Success metrics: 30% reduction in first-response tickets for pilot merchant OR NPS delta + precision > 0.7 on triage routing.
Rollout: start hosted Redwood (2 weeks), instrument logs + quality checks → if data isolation concerns, move to Dedicated private pool week 3–4.
Pricing: pilot credit-based (we cover first 20k tokens + dev hours), then standard per-token or transition to monthly committed Dedicated.

OBJECTIONS / RISKS + REBUTTALS (notes to use on calls)
- Objection: "We can't send customer PII to third-party hosted models."
  Rebuttal: Redwood Private (VPC) & Dedicated keep inference in their VPC; we can show architecture diagram and KMS integration. Offer redaction + allowlist approach for initial pilot.
- Objection: "Procurement timeline is long"
  Rebuttal: Start with scoped PoC under existing MSA (non-production) and use statement-of-work for pilot; present SOW template to legal to accelerate.
- Objection: "We already have an internal recommender"
  Rebuttal: Focus pilot on a non-core flow (support) to prove ROI. Emphasize speed to value and no-forced migration.

OUTREACH CADENCE (cold -> nurture)
Email 1 (intro): quick problem statement (ticket volume + ops drag), 1-sentence value prop, ask for 20-min discovery.
Email 2 (case): short case study + suggested pilot outline and timeline + ask for introduction to Eng/Product.
Email 3 (push): pricing example + offer to run a free quality eval on a synthetic prompt set.
LinkedIn InMail: keep <50 words, call out mutual connections (if any), invite to 20-min.
Follow-ups: mix email + 1 choreographed slack DM (if company public slack).

CALL SCRIPT — discovery (first 20 minutes)
- Intros (2 min).
- Goal question: "What would success look like after 6 weeks?" (listen for hard metrics).
- Current flows: ask about ticket types, search KPIs, catalog onboarding pain.
- Tech barriers: where is data stored, any air-gapped customers, infra/ops team capacity?
- Security: Compliance requirements? PCI/hipaa? Audit logs needed?
- Decision process & timeline: who else needs to sign off?
- Next milestone: align on pilot scope + quick PoC plan + dates.

QUALITY & EVALS (practical)
- Need 200–500 representative support tickets (anonymized) + golden labels for triage.
- For search/rerank pilot: sample of 1k queries + conversion labels (clicks/purchases).
- Maintain a shared spreadsheet for prompts / examples (team: g2m + eng).

BACK-OF-ENVELOPE PRICING (for initial convo)
- Pilot (6 weeks) estimate: 20k–50k tokens / week depending on volume. Offer $X in credits (internal).
- Post-pilot: if low-latency real-time assistant -> Dedicated reserved pool estimate = $Y/mo for X qps (need infra ask to get exact).
(note: fill $ with finance once we have traffic numbers)

INTERNAL ACTION ITEMS (Priya)
- [ ] Draft one-pager pilot SOW template with legal (due 2025-02-24).
- [ ] Build synthetic eval set for support triage (Sofia) — 200 tickets by 2025-02-22.
- [ ] Intro email template for Marissa (Liam to review).
- [ ] Architecture diagram showing Hosted vs Private flow (Daniel Park will need this).
- [ ] Schedule discovery call — target week of 2/24.

NOTES TO SELF / WIP IDEAS
- Could propose hybrid: inference in Dedicated but logging to hosted analytics (if they accept). Need to confirm data residency constraints.
- If they push for on-prem, flag as high-touch sale (eng resources + Professional Services).
- Prepare 1–2 short quote snippets from similar customers (anonymized) about ticket reduction and time-to-live.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (to answer before discovery)
- Do they have any existing NDA templates? (legal ask)
- Which merchants run on-prem vs cloud? impact on pilot scope.
- Volume estimate: avg tickets / day for pilot merchant.
- Who on their side owns procurement for third-party infra (legal / IT contact)?

END NOTES (scratch)
- Keep outreach conversational, avoid heavy infra talk in cold email. Lead with outcomes.
- Use Rowan (solutions eng) as technical backup on discovery call.

-----

Liam: "We should offer free eval credits to reduce friction"
Priya: "I'll lead outreach -- want to get Marissa on a quick call to scope pilot"
